hints: Each student can be matched with at most one partner, and each partner with at most one student.
Create a bipartite graph from students to acceptable partners.
Maximum bipartite matching can be found with augmenting paths; reroute earlier matches when necessary.
analogy: Assign a student to a partner; if that partner is occupied, try moving the current match elsewhere.
example: If student 1 accepts A,B and student 2 accepts A, a maximum assignment is 1-B and 2-A, not just 1-A.
algorithm: Use DFS augmenting paths for each student with a visited-partner array; if a partner is free or its current student can be rematched, assign it. Print matched pairs.
correctness: An augmenting path increases the matching size by one while preserving existing one-to-one constraints; when no such path remains, the matching is maximum.
complexity: O(nm) time with simple DFS and O(n+m) space.
